title: ModelMetadata
description: Preprocessing + inference-time constants paired with a deployed model artifact (typically the ONNX file). Captures everything the runtime needs that is NOT encoded in the ONNX graph itself: expected sample rate, expected trace length, per-channel normalization, decision threshold, model artifact hash, training provenance. Cross-language: consumed by Python (training-eval parity) and C++ (TensorRT inference). Schema version 1.0.

schema_version.description: Versioned schema identifier. Consumers MUST refuse unknown major versions.

created_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at export time.

model_artifact.description: Reference to the model file this metadata pairs with. Lives next to the artifact on disk (e.g., 'best.onnx' + 'best.model_metadata.json').

filename.description: Filename relative to this metadata file (e.g., 'best.onnx', 'engine.plan'). Resolver joins this with the directory of the metadata file.

framework.description: Artifact format. ONNX is the portable form; TensorRT is the deployment-platform-specific engine; PyTorch is the checkpoint format used during training.

sha256.description: Content hash of the artifact for tamper detection. Optional but strongly recommended for deployed models.

size_bytes.description: Artifact size in bytes. Optional; primarily for sanity-checking against the on-disk file.

input.description: Expected input tensor spec. The ONNX graph itself encodes shape; this section is the deployment-time documentation of what the model assumes, used for sanity-checking incoming data before dispatch.

name.description: ONNX input tensor name (e.g., 'signal'). Matches the ONNX graph's input.

items.description: One dimension of the input tensor. Integer for a fixed size, or the string '?' for a dynamic (typically batch) dimension.

shape.description: Tensor shape. Integer for fixed dims, '?' (string) for dynamic dims (typically the batch axis). Example for a 1D 1-channel single-trace model: ['?', 1, 512].
Output tensor shape. Example for a single-logit binary classifier: ['?', 1].

semantics.description: What the output value means. 'binary_logit' means apply sigmoid to get P(positive); 'binary_probability' means the value is already sigmoid-applied. Multi-class variants are equivalent for softmax/log-softmax outputs.

preprocessing.description: Signal-conditioning constants the runtime applies before inference, in the order listed here. Must match the preprocessing used during training; mismatch will silently degrade performance.

expected_fs_hz.description: Sampling rate the model was trained at (Hz). Inference inputs at a different rate must be resampled before invocation.

expected_trace_samples.description: Per-trace length in samples the model expects. Must match the time-axis dimension in input.shape.

items.description: A band-edge frequency in Hz. The two-element array is [low, high]; both must be positive.

bandpass_hz.description: Band-pass filter edges in Hz [low, high] applied at inference. Should match the bank's band_hz.

normalization.description: Per-channel signal normalization. For a 1-channel bipolar model the arrays are length 1. The scheme determines which fields are required: 'zscore' needs mean+std; 'minmax' would need min+max (add in a future schema version); 'none' needs neither.

items.description: Per-channel mean value applied as the centering constant during normalization.

mean.description: Per-channel mean (required for 'zscore'). Length must equal the input channel count.

items.description: Per-channel standard deviation applied as the scaling divisor during normalization. Must be strictly positive.

std.description: Per-channel standard deviation (required for 'zscore'). Length must equal the input channel count.

decision.description: Decision-rule constants applied to the model output to produce a class label.

threshold.description: Decision threshold applied to P(fibrotic). 0.5 unless calibration analysis recommends otherwise. For multi-class models this is the threshold for the positive class; multi-class extension may add per-class thresholds in a future schema version.

items.description: A human-readable class name. Position in the array matches the model output index.

class_labels.description: Human-readable class labels in the order matching the model's output index. For binary: ['healthy', 'fibrotic'] (index 0 = healthy, index 1 = fibrotic).

training_provenance.description: Where this model came from. Well-known keys: 'run_id' (identifier into the run.json that documents the training), 'run_json_path' (path to the run.json), 'training_bank_path' (path to the synthetic bank used for training), 'training_bank_schema_version' (the synthetic_bank schema version this bank conforms to, e.g. '1.0'), 'git_sha' (source repo state at training time). Additional keys are allowed for producer-specific provenance.

Dtype.description: Floating-point element dtype. Used for both input and output tensors.
